context: Request: all the firm's closed M&A deals whose executed agreements include indemnification sections (for a clause bank). Rubric: fifteen matters, each with its executed agreement (e.g. 1006-00007 executed-apa-proshield, 1015-00004 contribution-agreement-execution, 1037-00006 stock purchase agreement), plus precision (1003-00004, 1007-00006, 1038-00008, 1036-00004 and similar are outside).

runs.failure_point: Its scans kept only M&A-named agreement files, dropping two deals with differently named executed agreements; it also left out a deal whose executed agreement and closing it had printed, and added an outside matter.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The broad path search at [18] reached every needed matter, but the scan at [32] and the candidate script at [52] only took files matching M&A agreement names, which dropped an asset deal with a non-standard agreement file name and a deal documented by a contribution agreement.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The scan review said the filename regex restricts which files are scanned; the agent ran a content-only count but kept screening from the filename candidates.

other_errors.why: Its scripts printed one needed matter's executed stock purchase agreement with indemnification text and its closing date (evidence seen at [53]-[81]), but the answer leaves it out without a stated reason.
The answer lists a real-estate portfolio acquisition outside the set as a qualifying closed M&A deal.

divergence: All three runs fail, and all miss the matter whose executed agreement is a contribution agreement. Its path surfaced in each run's first broad path search, but a narrower agreement-name pattern written next dropped it: T0's second path search and T2's filename-filtered scan (over-narrow filters, first errors), while T1 widened its patterns, saw that agreement listed at [40], did not open it in screening (first error) and lost it again in a final scan whose agreement regex left it blank. T2 also dropped an asset deal whose executed agreement has a non-standard file name and left out a matter whose executed agreement and closing date its own scripts had printed. All three answers add matters outside the set. Reviews flagged the name-based filters in T0 (generically) and T2 (specifically, after which the agent ran a content scan but kept screening from filename candidates); no review named the omitted matters.
